reason: The text describes Moses and Aaron requesting that Pharaoh release the Hebrew slaves so they may go into the wilderness to worship their God (celebrated through sacrifice). The narrative concerns liberation from bondage through negotiation and divine intervention (the plagues), not military conflict or territorial sovereignty. The Hebrews are enslaved in Egypt and seeking temporary religious freedom, not fighting for control or sovereignty over land. This passage predates any Israelite settlement in Canaan.
